question_type: multi-issue narrative extraction (12 auction paragraphs across four March issues) -> quarterly averages -> OLS slope
decisive_step: Recognising that 'Treasury Financing Operations reports' names the narrative section 'TREASURY FINANCING OPERATIONS, OCTOBER-DECEMBER <yr>' printed in the March issue of the following year (treasury_bulletin_1988_03.txt:1688 with 'Auction of 2-Year Notes' at :1692/:1738/:1762, and likewise 1989_03:1755, 1990_03:1677, 1991_03:1656), and that 'tenders accepted' is the 'of which $X million was accepted' figure of the auction paragraph, excluding the 'In addition to ... accepted from Federal Reserve banks / Government accounts' add-ons. The reference made this at worklog Step 1 (parse) and Step 3 (grep for 'financing operations' in 1988_03 -> line 1688), and explicitly rejected table PDO-3 'Amount issued' as a source because its basis includes the add-ons in some years (worklog Steps 9-13; solution.structured.json key_decisions). Every GLM cell instead took table PDO-3 (a/b/c: 'Amount issued', b2: 'Amount tendered'), so all four are >25% off.

a.path_summary: Searched find_tables for the question's nouns (a[6],[8],[10]) and 'Treasury Financing Operations' (a[8]) which returned only FFO-1 token matches and TOC entries; settled on PDO-3 (a[12]-[23]). Spent ~880 steps paging raw PDO-3 parts across 1987_12..2001_03, chasing 'latest printing' per auction-date row with printings (a[58]-[86], [302]-[321]) and hitting OCR-shifted rows (a[79]-[83], [307]-[311]). Looped an 8-command cycle ~22 times (a[88]-[264]), then restarted three times from compaction summaries (a[265], [664], [853]). At a[323]/[700]/[899] it computed slopes for both PDO-3 columns ('tendered' vs 'issued') with calc and answered the 'Amount issued' slope; ~39% high because PDO-3 'Amount issued' includes Fed/foreign add-ons in 1987, 1989 and 1990 but not in 1988.

first_divergence.what_it_did: After find_tables 'Treasury Financing Operations' (a[8]) returned nothing relevant, it searched 'Public Offerings of Marketable Securities' and adopted PDO-3 as the source; from then on the only question it asked was which PDO-3 column ('Amount tendered' vs 'Amount issued') is meant (a[19],[89],[324],[706]).
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: The reference grepped the corpus text for 'financing operations' / '2-year note' and read the narrative auction paragraphs in the four March issues (worklog Step 3-8), taking the 'was accepted' figure of each auction and cross-checking it against noncompetitive + competitive sub-totals.

tool_use.friction: show_table on PDO-3 parts returned 'page rows 0-0 of 0' with --long/--grep (a[14],[16],[41],[272]-[276],[282],[859]) because dates are m/d/yy labels and the parser misaligned columns (a[36],[43]); printings --row in ISO form (1987-10, 1987-10-27, 1987-11-18) found nothing (a[21],[37],[39],[280],[292],[861],[881],[885]) and only the raw '10/21/87' label form worked (a[43]); printings --row 11/28/89 matched a 5-year row (a[67]); a zsh '===' glob error (a[72]); rg output truncated (a[61]); OCR-corrupted 1991_09/1991_12/1992_12 rows made the 'latest printing' differ from earlier ones (a[63],[79],[307]); an 8-step loop repeated ~22 times a[88]-[264] and three compaction restarts (a[265],[664],[853]); 3342 s, 463 requests, 55 M input tokens.

At b[9] it decided the source is 'likely a table', found PDO-3 (b[13]), read raw PDO-3 rows for the 2-year notes (b[17]-[29]) and at b[20] explicitly weighed 'narrative lines ... tenders accepted in auction process' against the table's 'Amount issued' and chose the table. calc slope at b[31]; submit accepted with no findings (b[33]).

smallest_change.change:
Index narrative section headings (upper-case lines such as 'TREASURY FINANCING OPERATIONS, OCTOBER-DECEMBER 1987' and their sub-headings 'Auction of 2-Year Notes') alongside tables, and have find_tables print them as '[section]' hits when the query words match a heading. For find_tables "Treasury Financing Operations" --years 1987-1991 the model would then have seen, above the FFO-1 token matches, e.g.:
  [section] TREASURY FINANCING OPERATIONS, OCTOBER-DECEMBER 1987 | treasury_bulletin_1988_03.txt:1688-1800 | match:title
      sub-headings: Auction of 2-Year Notes (:1692), 52-Week Bills (:1700), ..., Auction of 2-Year Notes (:1738), Auction of 2-Year and 4-Year Notes (:1762)
  [section] TREASURY FINANCING OPERATIONS, OCTOBER-DECEMBER 1988 | treasury_bulletin_1989_03.txt:1755-1900 | ...
  (and the 1990_03 / 1991_03 sections)
plus a hint line when a query returns 0 table parts: 'no table matched; N narrative sections match these words - see [section] lines or rg the phrase in upper case'. Optionally add `show_section <file> <line>` that prints the section text with line numbers (equivalent to sed -n, but discoverable). The heading exists in 51 issues of the corpus, so the index is a generic heading scan, not a per-question rule.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely - section hits appear only when the query words match a heading, and are printed as a separate '[section]' block above table groups; on questions that are table-based the block is empty. Slight page-budget cost when headings and table titles share words (e.g. 'Summary of Fiscal Operations').

alternatives.change: Add to the OfficeQA notes: 'A question that names a *report* or *section* ("Treasury Financing Operations", "Auction of ...") may point to narrative text, not a table. Before picking a table, run rg -n -i "<the phrase>" on the corpus and read the section heading and paragraphs (sed -n) in the issue that covers the period; in auction paragraphs the value "tenders accepted" is the "of which $X million was accepted" figure, and the "In addition to ... Federal Reserve" amounts are excluded.'
alternatives.why_not_first: a already had text telling it to match the question's wording and still framed the search as table selection (a[8],[12]); b and b2 did grep the narrative and were defeated by head -100 / -m 10 truncation (b[8], b2[44],[48]) and by an interpretation that included the add-ons (b[20]). A visible section hit in the tool output is a stronger nudge than another sentence, and the second half of the sentence (excluding add-ons) is officeqa_specific.

alternatives.change: Make show_table and printings work on PDO-3-style date-labelled tables: accept --row in m/d/yy, yyyy-mm-dd and yyyy-mm forms, filter by a 'Period to final maturity' value (--match '2y'), and flag rows whose numeric columns shifted relative to the sibling printing (the 1991_09/1991_12 OCR shifts that c[45] and b2[59] hit).

fix.why_not_text: Cell a had the full advice text and followed the applicable sentences (search by key nouns, prefer matching title/headers, use latest printing) - they steered it *toward* PDO-3, because the text and the tools both assume the answer lives in a table. b2 also had the text. The blind spot is in what find_tables can show: all four cells searched the exact question phrase 'Treasury Financing Operations' with find_tables (a[8], b[10], b2[8], c[8]) and got only FFO-1 token matches and TOC rows, so no sentence about matching wording could have surfaced the section. b and b2 even grepped the narrative (b[8], b2[44],[48]) and were defeated by output truncation and by the 'includes Fed allotments' interpretation (b[20]) rather than by lack of instruction.
fix.irreducible: Not irreducible: the reference solved it with high confidence and its answer is robust to the two December typo conflicts (sensitivity in worklog Steps 15-18). The question wording ('auction amount tenders accepted') is awkward but the Bulletin's own phrase 'tenders accepted in the auction process' matches it.

notes: 1) find_tables is blind to narrative sections: the query 'Treasury Financing Operations' (the literal source named by the question) returned FFO-1 'Summary of Fiscal Operations' by token match plus TOC rows in all four cells; the corpus has 51 issues with a 'TREASURY FINANCING OPERATIONS' heading, and 'Auction of 2-Year Notes' sub-headings, so a heading index is cheap. 2) PDO-3 is a trap on three axes: its 'Amount issued' basis includes Fed/foreign add-ons in some years and not others (reference worklog Step 9-13), its date row labels defeat printings' period matching unless typed as '10/21/87', and its 1991_09/1991_12/1992_12 printings have OCR-shifted rows that show_table does not mark (c[45],[53]; a[79],[307]; b2[59]) - so the 'latest printing' rule actively selects corrupted cells there. 3) The two rg-based cells (b[8], b2[44],[48]) had the right text within reach and lost it to head -100 / -m 10 truncation; a section tool or a 'grep with --files-with-matches then read' habit would have avoided that. 4) a's three compaction restarts each began from a summary that already said 'PDO-3', so compaction locked in the wrong source; the post-compaction summaries also carried a copy error (a[701]: the Q4-1990 average in the handoff summary did not match its own components - 'summary ... likely typo'). 5) The 8000-byte page cut hit find_tables '2-year notes' --all (b[6]) - a query with a table-like phrase but no --years fills the page with 1940s tables.
